clue.text: It is fair that I am with father at the new trial

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm, written without the apostrophe
pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of trial are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone argues that it is only just for them to join their father at a retrial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes RTIAL from TRIAL, which follows IM and PA. 'It is' and 'that' only join the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fair means judging without favour or bias towards either side.

clue.text: Aimed to reform newspapers, radio and television

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters of aimed are put into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to overhaul the press and broadcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges the five letters of AIMED.
explanation.definitionFit: The press and broadcasters together are collectively called the mass communication outlets of a country.

clue.text: Break law, say, at all times

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it, so the letters of law and say are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A rebel who boasts of breaking the law, for example, constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' reads as an instruction to law-breakers, but it scrambles the six letters of LAW and SAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at every moment happens constantly, forever, without exception.

clue.text: Emotional shock in Sumatra strangely headed off

indicators.note: strangely says the remaining letters appear in an odd new order
headed off means the word loses its head, its first letter

explanation.surface: A traveller in Indonesia suffers a mental blow and wanders off in a strange direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headed off' strips the S from SUMATRA, leaving UMATRA, and 'strangely' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychological wound or deeply distressing experience is a medical sense of the word.

clue.text: Something wrong with a young lady

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Something is not right about a certain girl.
explanation.definitionFit: When things are awry or faulty, we say there is something not right, out of order.

clue.text: Trouble there would be when Satan has to foot the bill

definitions.text: Trouble there would be when Satan has to foot the bill

parts.words: Trouble there would be when Satan has to foot the bill
parts.note: an idiom for serious trouble, pictured literally as the Prince of Darkness being made to settle a debt

explanation.surface: A joke about hell's chief being handed the restaurant bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means serious trouble will follow; the clue reads it literally as the devil paying a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom warning that serious trouble or punishment will follow.

clue.text: Something to get married for

parts.note: recalls the wedding vow in which a couple promise to stay together through good times and bad

explanation.surface: A question of what reason anyone has for marrying.
explanation.walkthrough: The traditional vows say 'for richer for poorer, for better for worse', so the phrase follows 'for' in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The marriage vow pledges loyalty through good fortune and bad alike.

clue.text: Some politicians follow transport catch

parts.note: to shadow someone is to follow them closely
a cab is a taxi, a form of transport
to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: Some politicians tail a taxi, hoping to catch it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the opposition's team of senior spokespeople, each watching a government minister, is so named.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition's front-bench team mirror government ministers, so they are a group of politicians.

clue.text: Uncomfortable, unwell but relaxing

parts.note: ill means unwell
at ease means relaxing, as when soldiers are told to stand easy

explanation.surface: Someone feels sick yet rests, a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contradiction ('but relaxing') only sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling awkward or anxious in company is feeling uncomfortable.

clue.text: Found a school

definitions.meaning: to found is to set up or establish, as a verb
an institution of learning, such as a technical college

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to establish an organisation; as a noun it names an academic or teaching body.

clue.text: New daily girl

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of daily are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: A fresh newspaper for a young woman, or a new cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New daily' suggests a newspaper, but 'New' rearranges DAILY into a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, as in the Bennet sister in Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Fully intending to return the money

indicators.note: to return is to turn back, so the word for money is read backwards

parts.note: notes are paper money

explanation.surface: Someone firmly plans to pay back the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' looks like repayment, but it turns NOTES backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are determined to do something, you are resolved upon it.

clue.text: Award for finding a ring by the cliff

parts.note: the letter O is round, like a ring
a scar is a steep rocky cliff, especially in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone is rewarded for discovering a ring lying near a clifftop.
explanation.walkthrough: A scar is a steep rock face, a word common in the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden statuette given by the Academy is the best-known film prize.

clue.text: Nothings holding a label in New Zealand

indicators.note: holding means the pair of letters for nothings clasps the word for label between them

parts.note: O looks like zero, so two nothings give two Os
a tag is a label attached to something

explanation.surface: A pair of zeros carrying a ticket while travelling in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names a place found in New Zealand: the southern region with Dunedin as its city.
explanation.definitionFit: A region of the South Island, a place located within that country.

clue.text: Long after getting key to the treasure

indicators.note: after getting says the word for long comes second, following the key

parts.note: C is a musical key
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Someone yearns after obtaining the key to the treasure chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is a musical key, C, not something that opens a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden store of valuables or a hoard is a buried stash.

clue.text: Again play your part and re spend

definitions.meaning: to play one's part once more, act again
to respond is to answer or behave in reply to something

explanation.definitionFit: Split re-act, it means perform again; as one word it means answer a stimulus.

clue.text: Coming into season

definitions.meaning: an arrival or appearance, as a noun
the church season of the four weeks before Christmas

explanation.definitionFit: It means an arrival, and is also the name of the period of preparation before Christmas in the church year.

clue.text: Liveliness of mischievous sprite

indicators.note: mischievous describes the letters of sprite misbehaving and getting jumbled

explanation.surface: A playful elf full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mischievous' rearranges SPRITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for vivacity, wit and spirited energy.

clue.text: Bill crashes vehicle in Africa

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: crashes means the vehicle's letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A man called Bill wrecks his car on an African road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is AC, an account; 'crashes' makes CRA from CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana's capital city is located on the west coast of that continent.

clue.text: Rough gale in part of London

indicators.note: rough describes the letters of gale and in tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A stormy wind blows through a district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' rearranges the letters of GALE and IN together. EALING is a district of west London, known for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough in west London famous for its film studios.

clue.text: The root of persuasion

parts.note: a vegetable root that is also the reward dangled in front of a donkey, as in the stick-and-reward approach

explanation.surface: The basic cause of all persuasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'root' suggests origin, but it means a root vegetable used as an incentive.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange root vegetable, and figuratively an incentive offered to persuade someone.

clue.text: Not concealed from new voter

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of voter are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Nothing is hidden from a first-time voter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges VOTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done openly and in plain view is not hidden.

clue.text: City is very nice without a rail way

indicators.note: without means the letters for railway are taken away

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A city that is lovely and has no train line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes RY, the abbreviation for railway, from VERYNICE. Venice is famous for having canals rather than roads.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian lagoon city famous for its canals and gondolas.

clue.text: Indent for vacation

definitions.meaning: a niche or alcove set back into a wall
a break when parliament or courts are not sitting

explanation.definitionFit: It means an alcove set back into a wall, and a break from work or parliamentary sittings.

clue.text: Plump for beer

definitions.meaning: plump means rather fat, as an adjective
a strong dark beer, like porter

explanation.definitionFit: It means portly or fat, and is a dark heavy kind of ale.

clue.text: Audacious attempt-to see if it fits

definitions.meaning: an attempt to deceive or get away with something cheeky, informal British usage
putting on clothes in a shop to check their size

explanation.definitionFit: Informally a cheeky attempt at deception; also the act of putting on a garment to check its size.

clue.text: Hit 150 before being dismissed

indicators.note: before places the Roman number ahead of the word for dismissed

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A cricketer scores 150 runs before getting out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a batsman's innings; OUT is the cricket word for dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy blow, or to strike someone hard.

clue.text: Article found in state water way

indicators.note: found in says the article sits inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news item discovered about a river in a certain country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts AN inside CAL, the short form of California.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial channel cut for boats or irrigation.

clue.text: Versatility of an octagon or enneagon perhaps

definitions.meaning: being adaptable and able to do many things

definitions.text: of an octagon or enneagon perhaps
definitions.meaning: describes shapes with eight or nine edges, a quality of having lots of faces

explanation.definitionFit: Having many abilities is figuratively having lots of facets, and literally polygons have lots of edges.

clue.text: Very strongly in round numbers, see

parts.note: tens are round numbers, multiples of ten
Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Something expressed forcefully in approximate figures, look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is not 'look' but a bishop's diocese: ELY, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with great force or fervour is doing it fiercely.
